extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and illustrative case-law examples for evaluating compliance with 35 U.S.C. §112 written description and enablement requirements (including §112, sixth paragraph/means-plus-function issues) during patent examination and prosecution. Focuses on when specifications provide sufficient structure/support and when claimed scope is commensurate with disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function corresponding structure requirement (§112, ¶6)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim limitation is in means-plus-function form the specification must disclose corresponding structure, material, or acts sufficient to perform the claimed function and must clearly link or associate that structure to the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification need only disclose sufficient structure to perform the function to one of ordinary skill in the art. If the function is not a specific one requiring a special program or algorithm, a general purpose computer with memory may be sufficient corresponding structure (e.g., for the function of storing data). The disclosure must prevent purely functional claiming by providing co-extensive structure as disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement (§112, ¶1) — possession
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must describe the claimed invention in sufficient detail that one skilled in the art can reasonably conclude that the inventor had possession of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the specification must be understandable to a person of ordinary skill and show that the inventor actually invented the claimed invention. Mere statement of a problem or desired result is insufficient; the disclosure must convey constructive possession of the claimed subject matter (illustrated by multiple case examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (§112, ¶1) — full scope without undue experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must teach those skilled in the art how to make and use the full scope of the claimed invention without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement must cover the full breadth of the claims. Even if some embodiments are enabled, claims are invalid if significant portions of the claimed scope require undue experimentation or are not taught by the specification (see AK Steel, Sitrick examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional claim limitations must be supported and commensurate in scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional language (describing a problem to be solved or a function/result achieved) must be adequately supported by the written description and commensurate in scope with the enabling disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional claim limitations that attempt to cover all means or methods of performing a function or solving a problem can render a claim overly broad if the specification does not support or enable that full breadth (per the 2011 Supplementary Guidelines and case law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot claim generically when specification discloses only a particular method
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that generically covers all ways of achieving a result is invalid if the specification only describes a particular method for achieving that result and does not show the inventor possessed the generic method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LizardTech: Claiming all ways of performing DWT-based compression to create a seamless DWT failed because the specification described only a single way (maintaining updated sums). The spec need not spell out every detail, but must include enough to convince a skilled person that the inventor possessed the generic invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot claim broader species/genus when other species are not shown to be attainable by routine methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims to a broader class (e.g., fully-human antibodies) are not supported if the specification discloses only different species (e.g., chimeric/mouse antibodies) and creation of the broader species was not routine or enabled at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centocor: Disclosure of a chimeric antibody with desirable properties did not support claiming fully-human antibodies with the same properties where it was not possible with conventional technology to create such fully-human antibodies at the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added later or broadened during prosecution must be supported by the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that were not part of the original disclosure (e.g., broader 'spikeless' claims added later) must nonetheless be supported by the specification; absence of such support can render them invalid under written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICU Med.: Spikeless claims were invalid where the original specification described only valves with spikes; figures and preslit embodiments that facilitate piercing did not demonstrate possession of spikeless valves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification teaching away can defeat enablement for portions of claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification expressly teaches against an embodiment or discourages certain parameters, that teaching can show that the specification does not enable a claimed embodiment and may require undue experimentation to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AK Steel: The specification warned that higher silicon content would not wet well, discouraging experimentation and showing lack of enablement for claims covering high-silicon coatings even though other coatings were enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must enable all embodiments encompassed by their breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims are broad enough to cover multiple types of embodiments (e.g., movies and video games), the specification must enable each embodiment within the claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sitrick: Although the spec described an IAIS for video games, it did not teach how to perform analogous substitution/integration in movies. Because movies and video games are technically different, enabling one does not necessarily enable the other; claims covering both require enabling disclosure for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: A specification that discloses multiple problems or multiple solutions may support claims directed to only one
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification sets out more than one problem or more than one solution to a problem, it is not necessary for every claim to include limitations addressing all disclosed problems/solutions; a claim addressing only one disclosed solution can satisfy written description if the disclosure conveys possession of that claimed solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revolution Eyewear and Crown Packaging examples: Claims directed to only one of several disclosed solutions (e.g., only the primary-frame magnetic solution; only the sloped chuck wall solution) were found to comply with written description where the spec supported that single solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-means claims are non-compliant with enablement (§112, ¶1) / combination requirement for §112, ¶6
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim drafted as a single means-plus-function limitation with no other limitations (i.e., not an element in a claim for a combination) fails the combination requirement of §112, ¶6 and does not comply with the enablement requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Hyatt: A 'single-means-claim' that embraces every conceivable structure for performing the function is not enabled because the specification only states those structures known to the inventor; means-plus-function limitations must be recited as an element in a combination to be proper under §112, ¶6.

rubrics_metrics.name: For biological sequence claims, actual isolation/characterization may be required to show written description
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims to DNA/proteins, merely describing the protein or antigen may be insufficient; the specification may need to disclose the nucleotide sequence or an isolation/characterization method to demonstrate possession of the claimed nucleic acid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiers (interference context): Lack of actual isolation/sequencing (or adequate descriptive support) led to failure to prove conception/possession. In some cases disclosure of a well-characterized antigen can suffice if creation of antibodies is routine, but where it was not routine, more specific disclosure is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle: specification need not spell out every detail but must convince skilled artisan and enable without undue experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification does not have to disclose every detail or every way to achieve the claimed result, but must include enough to convince one of ordinary skill that the inventor possessed the invention and taught how to make and use it across the full claimed scope without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated across cases: courts permit some breadth where reasonable extrapolation is routine, but will reject claims that claim all solutions to a problem when spec shows only one solution or that require significant additional inventive work to achieve other species.
